gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Anker's own US store lists the SOLIX S2000 at $999.99 today (2026-11-15). Every source it used reported the $699.99 sale, so ChatGPT's 'mainstream pick' now costs about $100 more than the BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 ($899) and about $120 more than the EcoFlow DELTA 3 Max ($879). Both of those rate 2,400 W or more of continuous output against the S2000's 1,500 W.
standout_why: Compared against outagereadyhq.com (cited), which gives the S2000 at $699.99 on Nov 12 and calls it the best value per Wh; gearjunkie.com (cited), which gives $700; powerstations.reviews/prices (cited), which gives $729.99 on Nov 9; and wattpowerstation.com (cited), which gives prices from Nov 9 and the C2000 Gen 2 at $999.99. None of them has today's maker prices. Two have gone up: S2000 to $999.99 and C2000 Gen 2 to $1,199.99. None lists the Growatt INFINITY 2000 PRO at $799 with a TT-30 outlet and 1,200 W solar input. None lists the AFERIY P210 'No App' at $659 on AFERIY's own store, which is under the $749 Walmart price ChatGPT showed. wattpowerstation does carry the tested usable Wh, so cost per usable Wh can already be worked out from a cited page. The new part is today's prices.
decides: The price finding confirms Dabbsson 2000L ($649, 1,887 Wh tested, $0.34 per usable Wh) as the cheapest per usable Wh. It removes the Anker S2000 from the value tier: at $999.99 it costs more than DELTA 3 Max ($879) and Elite 200 V2 ($899), and it has only 1,500 W continuous output and 400 W solar input. For RV buyers, Growatt INFINITY 2000 PRO at $799 is the cheapest model here with a TT-30 outlet. The Anker C2000 Gen 2, the other one with TT-30, is $1,199.99.
